sentences.text:
1 2. By the impugned award, learned Claims Tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.16,45,000/- to the appellants/claimants on account of death of deceased- Achintya Jha, husband of appellant-1, father of appellants-2 and 3, and son of appellant-4, who died in motor accident took place on 24.06.2018 by rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, Innova Car bearing registration No.CG-04 CT-9000, driven by respondent-1, owned by respondent-2, and insured by the Insurance Company,
respondent-3.
3.
As per the pleadings, the deceased-Achintya Jha was working as Document Writer in the Tahsil Office, Raipur, and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
He was highly qualified, having B.Com Degree, PG Diploma in Computer Application from the CV Raman University, and had also passed Typing and Shorthand examination.
The appellants/claimants are dependents on the income of the deceased.

4. Respondents-1 and 2, driver and owner of the offending vehicle have proceeded ex parte, and not contested the claim.
5. Respondent-3 Insurance Company contested the claim of the claimants before the Claims Tribunal by submitting their written statement and pleaded that at the time of accident, driver of the offending vehicle was not having any valid and effective driving license with him, and there is breach of Policy conditions, and therefore, Insurance Company is not liable to pay compensation to the claimants.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, learned Tribunal has framed five issues and after appreciating the material available on record, decided Mac 1059 of 2020 the same in favour of the appellants/claimants, and the Tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- per month and awarded the compensation amount accordingly.
7.

Shri Uttam Pandey, learned counsel for the appellants would submit that the deceased was aged about 42 years on the date of accident and was working as Document Writer at Tahsil Office,
Raipur.

He was highly qualified, and was having B.Com Degree, PG Diploma in Computer Application from the CV Raman University, and had also passed Typing and Shorthand examination, thereby, his monthly income of Rs.10,000/-, assessed by the Tribunal, is on the lower side.
In view of his qualification and profession, the tribunal ought to have considered his income as Rs.15,000/- per month.
He would further submit that the Tribunal has awarded very low amount on other conventional heads.
Therefore, total compensation amount is liable to be enhanced suitably.

8. On the other hand, Shri Ghanshyam Patel, learned counsel for the Insurance Company would support the award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal, and would submit that the claimants have not produced any document regarding income of the deceased that he actually working as Document Writer at the Tahsil Office, Raipur.

Although he was possessing the PG Diploma in Computer application, and other credentials, but the same itself cannot be considered that he was earning higher amount than the amount as considered by the Tribunal.
The amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is fully justified, which needs no interference by this court.

Smt. Preeti vs Bharat Soni on 14 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92964663/
2 Mac 1059 of 2020 9.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

10. Barring the oral evidence of the appellants/claimants, though no document relating to the income of the deceased has been filed by the claimants, but the documents relating to his educational qualification as well as technical qualification have been produced by the claimants vide Ex.P7 to Ex.P11.
From perusal of the documents produced by the claimants, it is quite vivid that deceased was a graduate from the Pt Ravi Shankar University, Raipur.
He was having the PG Diploma in Computer application from the CV Raman University, Bilaspur and also having technical qualification of Typing and Shorthand.
Therefore, consideration of the Claims Tribunal that the deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month appears to be on lower side.

However, looking to the educational and professional qualification of the deceased, and nature of his job; this Court is of the view that Rs.12,000/- would be the appropriate monthly income of the appellant, which is to be taken in the present case.

11. In light of above, and taking guidance from the decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Magma General Insurance Company Limited v. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and Others (2018) 18 SCC 130 and in case of Smt Sarla Verma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others (2009) 6 SCC 121, this court is recomputing the compensation as below:
Income of the claimant is being taken as Rs.12,000/- per month, and Rs.1,44,000/-
per annum (12000 x 12) Mac 1059 of 2020 By adding 25% of the income towards future prospects as has been considered in case of Pranay Sethi (supra), annual income of the deceased comes to Rs.1,80,000/- {144000 + (144000 x 40/100)}.

(135000 x 14).
In view of decisions of Hon'ble Supreme Court in cases of Pranay Sethi (supra) and Shri Ram General Insurance Company Limited Vs Bhagat Singh Rawat and others (Civil Appeals-2410-2412/2023 @ SLP(C)-11669- 11671/2020), decided on March 27, 2023, Rs.40,000/- Spousal consortium , Funeral expenses-15,000/-, Loss of estate-Rs.15,000/- and 10% enhancement in every three years comes to Rs.84,000/- (40000 + 15000 + 15000 + 14000 (70000 x 20/100).

For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is allowed in part.
The amount of compensation of Rs.16,45,000/- already awarded by the Tribunal is now enhanced to Rs.19,74,000/-.
Thereby, the claimants are entitled for additional amount of Rs.3,29,000/- (1974000  1645000).
the additional amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim application till its realization.
The impugned award stands modified to the extent indicated herein above.
13. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation enhanced by this Court within a period of 60 days from today.

On such deposit by the Insurance Company,
Rs.2,00,000/- shall be deposited in name of appellants- 2 and 3 for a period of five years in Mac 1059 of 2020 Fixed Deposit at any Nationalized bank.
Remaining amount shall be paid to the appellants/claimants through Bank transaction/Account payee cheque.
14. Appeal is partly allowed to the extent as indicated herein above.
15. No order as to costs.
